why_this_matters: Day 44 sits in Phase 3 (NumPy + Scientific Computing), whose goal is: Manipulate n-dimensional arrays fast, and understand the maths they implement. Today's core material - Why pseudo-randomness is reproducible, np.random.default_rng and Generator, Distributions: uniform, normal, binomial, poisson - is the vocabulary the rest of the phase is built on. Learners who skip the concept and jump to copying code usually stall two weeks later; the goal here is that you can explain what you did, not just that it ran.

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Generating example datasets with different distributions
np.random.seed(0)  # For reproducibility

# Normal distribution data
normal_data = np.random.normal(loc=0, scale=1, size=1000)

# Uniform distribution data
uniform_data = np.random.uniform(low=-2, high=2, size=1000)

# Exponential distribution data
exponential_data = np.random.exponential(scale=1, size=1000)

# Plotting the distributions
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))

# Normal Distribution Plot
plt.subplot(3, 1, 1)
plt.hist(normal_data, bins=30, color='skyblue', alpha=0.7)
plt.title('Normal Distribution')
plt.xlabel('Value')
plt.ylabel('Frequency')

# Uniform Distribution Plot
plt.subplot(3, 1, 2)
plt.hist(uniform_data, bins=30, color='lightgreen', alpha=0.7)
plt.title('Uniform Distribution')
plt.xlabel('Value')
plt.ylabel('Frequency')

# Exponential Distribution Plot
plt.subplot(3, 1, 3)
plt.hist(exponential_data, bins=30, color='salmon', alpha=0.7)
plt.title('Exponential Distribution')
plt.xlabel('Value')
plt.ylabel('Frequency')

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

common_mistakes.mistake: Watching the lecture without running the repository notebook.
common_mistakes.why: Recognition is not recall: code that looked obvious fails the moment you type it yourself.
common_mistakes.fix: For every topic today, run the linked notebook cell, then retype it from memory in your own file.

common_mistakes.mistake: Using Why pseudo-randomness is reproducible on data whose types or shape you have not printed.
common_mistakes.why: Most failures in this topic are input problems (dtype, shape, missing values) rather than logic errors.
common_mistakes.fix: Print type and shape immediately before the operation; keep that habit for all 275 days.

debugging.symptom: The linked notebook cell raises ModuleNotFoundError or ImportError.
debugging.cause: Wrong kernel/environment selected, or the library is not installed in the active environment.
debugging.fix: Print sys.executable in the notebook and install into that environment (Day 4).

debugging.symptom: Your output differs from the recording even though the code looks identical.
debugging.cause: Library version differences, a changed default argument, or unseeded randomness.
debugging.fix: Pin versions (requirements.txt), set a random seed, and compare dtypes and shapes, not just values (Day 5).
